label: text
text: About 150 missionaries from the province of Kwang tung gathered at St. Paul's College Hostel this morning to review their position in view of recent developments in China as a result of which they were obliged to leave the sphere of their activities. Local missions were also represented.

label: text
text: The Press were not invited to the meeting but a "China Mail" representative who conversed after the meeting with its Chairman (Mr. G. H. McNeur, New Zealand Presbyterian Mission, Canton) was informed that no definite policy had been decided upon. The meeting had been called with the object of interchange of information as to the situation and its relation to the position of the chirebes represented.

label: text
text: "The aged for a united policy had been felt, said Dr. McNeur and there had been no distinction of denomination or nationality" in the representation at the meeting. The general feeling had been that the Chinese Christian churches were in a position now to stand by themselves if they so desired and if they wished missionary activity to cease the missionaries were prepared to leave.

label: text
text: A small committee had been authorised to go into the position, said Mr. McNeur; meanwhile there would be no question of sending missionaries home unless forlough was outstanding.

label: text
text: The Committee appointed with power to co-opt were Dr. Creighton off the True Light Middle School (American Presbyterian). Rev. W. W. Clavson (London Missionary Society, Canton) and the Rev. C. Sheep (United Brethren Mission, Canton).

label: text
text: The chief item of interest in regard to the launch is that other duties have called away Capt. Tossins and "command" has been taken over by Captain Kendall. Quite a large number travelled over on Saturday and there will probably be a full ship on Monday (to-day) as many missionaries will be going over to attend a special conference at St. Paul's Hostel to discuss the present situation. The matter was brought up at the close of the service on Sunday evening; there was a large attendance.

label: text
text: The 19th was the anniversary of the opening of the Hall but no special reference was made of the fact. A concert was to have been held on Saturday, but owing to the unsettled weather conditions it has been postponed till the following Saturday. An interesting programme is expected to be presented.

label: text
text: The Food Committee is carrying on their service in a satisfactory manner and the thanks of the community are due to all who shoulder the burden of this work.

label: text
text: The roads suffered a great deal from the heavy rains, but good progress has been made in the repairing of the damage.

label: text
text: Considerable difficulty was experienced in getting the launch of this morning (Monday) owing to the pumps being out of order. At 9 o'clock a start was made.

label: text
text: Shanghai, July 18.—The Police yesterday arrested a Romanian named Alex Gregorenko in connection with the alleged attempted bribery of the policeman Kedrolivansky. Gregorenko appeared at the Mixed Court this morning and was remanded until Monday on bail of $5,000; but this was not forthcoming.—Reuter.

label: text
text: The s.s. Tung On. which arrived back from Kongnoon yesterday afternoon, sailed for Canton this morning with more supplies. Her trip to Kongnoon was uneventful except that she was aground for some hours on the Wangmun Bar and was not re-floated until H.M.S. Moorhen rendered assistance with the supply of a lighter for emptying the bunkers. Six European passengers were brought from Kongnoon.

label: text
text: Owing to the registration of numbers of seamen, the shipping situation has considerably improved and there will shortly be nothing to hinder ships with cargo to carry, moving from their anchorage. The Hai Ning, of the Douglas Steamship Company, has already done so and is now at her wharf taking on cargo, chiefly American Naval stores.

label: text
text: The harbour is gradually assuming a more normal appearance and many more launches are noticed to be in operation. Engineers and coxswains for the harbour launches have been engaged in considerable numbers and others have applied to the Police for employment. The War Department launches have maintained a service since the beginning of the strike and by an unfortunate coincidence there were mishaps to both this week-end. As a result of going aground at Green Island the Tommy Atkins sustained damage to her bows, part of the stem piece having been torn away. The Umphali has been refloated after having been aground for some days.

label: text
text: Almost as many motor boats and walla walls are now available both sides of the harbour as there were in normal times, charges being the same.

label: text
text: warship movements during the week-end have been the departure of H.M.S. Diomede for Home and H.M.S. Concord for the north to join the fleet. The French gunboat Argol sailed for Canton, and the U.S. destroyer Simpson for an unknown destination. Vessels still in harbour are H.M.S. Titania and Submarine L.33, H.M.A.S. Brisbane, and the U.S. Ships Asheville and Bulmer.

label: text
text: The-Duke-of-Comnaught unveiled the Machine Gun Corps memorial in the open space between the Mall gates, and St. George's Hospital, Grosvenor-place, W. on May 10. The memorial, sculptured by Mr. F. Derwent Wood, R.A., shows the bronze figure of David, more than Sft. high, leaning on Goliath's sword. The figure stands on a base of Mazzano stone, and on each side are shown laurel-wreathed machine-guns.

label: text
text: The Duke chatted with four members of the corps who had won the Victoria Cross—Major J. R. N. Graham, Captain A. E. Kerr, Lieutenant W. A. White, and Corporal A. H. Cross—and inspected the guard of honour formed of former members of the M.G.C., now in the Royal Tank Corps.

label: text
text:
The Duke recalled that 1,120 officers and 12,671 other ranks of the corps were killed in the war, 2,881 officers and 45,377 other ranks being wounded, missing, or taken prisoner. The casualties were more than a quarter of the total strength.
As the National Anthem was played, it was sung by the large crowd. Many women cried, and several relatives of dead members of the corps were helped into St. George's Hospital in a fainting condition.

label: text
text: Hundreds of men and women pressed forward to lay their wreaths besides the larger one sent by the corps, and the police had to link hands to regulate the movement.

label: text
text: Dayton, July 18.—Little evidence, up to the present has been taken in the Scopes case; most of the time having been taken up with arguments on legal points.—Mr. Ryan, finally objected to the admission of the evidence of scientists, Judge Raulston allowed the point, which will thus exclude the testimony of experts, many of whom had travelled hundreds of miles to testify on behalf of Scopes. Angry on bursts greeted the ruling.—Reuter's American Service.

label: text
text: Peking, July 19.—The vernacular papers state that the headquarters of Tuan Chi-jui have received a wire from Bhensi reporting that Sun Yuh's forces have defeated Wuh Sin-tien and entered Bianfu.—Reuter.

label: text
text: A sensation was caused at the conclusion of the Amateur Athletic Association's championship meeting at Stamford Bridge, for which there was a strong foreign entry. The Secretary, at the presentation of trophies, stated that two medals earned by the American Murchison for winning the 100 and 200 yards' events must be withheld pending investigation into his amateur status. Murchison was informed of the matter before the meeting began. It is understood the question concerns the alleged payment of expenses.

text: In an article in the “Daily News,” Mr. A. G. Gardiner writes:—

label: text
text: Hobbs has won a place in the gallery of modern celebrities as the supreme exponent of the whole range of the batsman's art. He could not be excluded from a list of household names, any more than could Bernard Shaw, Charlie-Chaplin,-or-Mr.-Lloyd George.

label: text
text: "He is a real link of Empire. In far-away Melbourne workers pour out in tides to see Hobbs more eagerly than to see a prince of the blood or a victor of the war."

label: text
text: Hobbs is a perfect and matchless artist. He is so easily the finest cricketer of our generation that it is unnecessary to look for a rival. He would have a place in the world's best team without a challenge.

label: text
text: "After the death of his father he set out with his bat to help his mother to bring up his 11 brothers and sisters.

label: text
text: "However bowlers may change their attack, however clever fields-men may be, Hobbs's amazing repertoire of strokes beats them. The world is now watching Hobbs overtaking Dr. W. G. Grace's mighty achievement, and awaits the day when Hobbs will plant his flag higher on the pinnacle of centuries."

text: Marshal Petain has arrived and begun work with the General Staff.

label: text
text: Reports from Fez state that enemy pressure on the centre, northern front is palpably slackening.

label: text
text: New attacks at Ainnastouf and Ainaicha posts were repulsed with heavy loss. There were no French casualties.

label: text
text: Generally speaking, the various districts are not meeting with great difficulty.

label: text
text: The Air Force is very busy reprovisioning stations and compelling assailants to flee precipitously.

label: text
text: The first detachments of the Moroccan division from Rhineland have arrived at Oujda.

label: text
text: A communique says the French have-lost posts at Babhosein, Wedbaumrin, after a violent Riff attack in which the Riffs lost heavily.

label: text
text: Marshall Petain met Marshal Lyautey at Rabat and later had an audience with the Sultan of Morocco. M. Naulin, interviewed before going to Morocco applauded the decision to send Marshal Petain to Morocco, as his presence there would cheer the troops. M. Naulin said there were at present 125,000 troops in the Riff region and he believed this force was adequate to achieve the French aims. Reports in the French Press of Riff activities in the direction of Fez are confirmed by a message from Madrid which describes Violent-Riff attacks on Ainicha and incessant aeroplane bombardments of the enemy lines.

label: text
text:
The Ganetzky, head of the Soviet delegation which is negotiating the Russo-German trade agreement, interviewed by the Rosta News Agency, said the negotiations are now almost ended. Only a few questions are unsettled.
He declared the Soviet agreed to make important concessions but the German Government demanded further concessions while not making a single concession itself; but the appointment of Count Brockdorf Frantzau to represent Germany seemed to prove Germany's realised importance of immediate conclusion of the treaty.

label: text
text: He was sure Germany would soon make concessions and with goodwill the treaty might be signed in a few days.

text: A military revolt, headed by a number of officers who were arrested after the outbreak on April 18 and who escaped from the fortress of San Juliao, broke out early in the morning.

label: text
text:
The cruiser Vasco da Gama de-
clared for the revolutionaries.

label: text
text: The Government took prompt measures to suppress the revolt, he leader of which is Captain Baptista. Four other officers have already surrendered and have been put in jail.

label: text
text:
The submission of the Vasco da Gama is momentarily expected.
Other revolutionaries are encamped near Bélem but the movement is considered already to be suppressed. A large force of troops is precautionarily guarding the President's Palace. All is quiet in the city.

label: text
text: All revolutionaries surrendered this morning after much shooting. Martial law has been established all over the country. The Government threatened to bombard the Vasco Da Gama if it held out after which the cruiser surrendered unconditionally. In the afternoon the situation is otherwise normal.
